Ἐφέσῳ τρέφων στερεωτέρᾳ τροφῇ, περὶ ὕψους καὶ μήκους καὶ πλάτους καὶ βά θους

βαθυτάτους ὑπάρχοντας, καὶ ἐκ φεύγοντας τὴν ἀνθρωπίνην κατάστασιν. Κάμινοι οἱ
πειρασμοί· διὰ γὰρ τῶν πειρασμῶν κα θάρας καὶ ἀκηλιδώτους τὰς καρδίας τῶν
ἐκλεκτῶν ὁ Θεὸς ἐκλέγεται. Ὁ αἱρετικὸς ὑπακούει γλώσσης τῆς τῶν ἀθέων δο
γμάτων· οἱ δὲ τῆς Ἐκκλησίας, οὐδὲ προσέχουσιν. ∆ιὰ τοῦ ὑπακούειν, τὸ ἑκούσιον
δείκνυσιν, ὡς εἰς τὴν τοῦ Θεοῦ σοφὴν διοίκησιν ἐξαμαρτών. –Οὗτος ὑπακούει ταῖς

pass_a_gloss:
Each brother receives spiritual knowledge as feeding varies; Paul gave milk to Corinthians, solid food to Ephesians discussing dimensions; these distinctions show the rational nature's division covering judgments and providence, deep and leading beyond humanity. Trials are furnaces; God chooses warm, sluggish hearts of the elect through trials. Heretic obeys godless doctrines' tongue; Church pays no heed. Obeying shows voluntariness as erring into God's wise rule. He obeys lawless tongues, receiving unjust calculations, hastening to act; righteous ignores them, seeing visible and invisible, not feeding self further. Faithful will see world's words presented as mental food; unbeliever knows no thing's word from soul's uncleanness; soul's wealth is God's knowledge, Paul teaches: enriched in all, all knowledge, all wisdom; if anyone wishes to show this conception is not mine, Let the wealthy say where they got their money—those who wandered in animal skins, poor, suffering, and oppressed. How can the unbeliever lack even a small coin when many faithless ones, dressed in great wealth—kings and rulers of this world—have abundant riches? Honest lips speak good thoughts; to the fool, evil thoughts are welcome. What share does justice have with injustice? Unless someone who repented seeks wisdom and faith. By justice we hide wrongdoing; by self-control, excess; by love, hate; by lack of greed, avarice—specifically 17.200. We also hide pride through humility, rashness through gentleness, seeking spiritual friendship that means holy knowledge; and per Paul, some saints are called fellow citizens and natives of the heavenly Jerusalem, built on the foundation of apostles and prophets. He says the body is the house of the soul, the soul the house of the mind, and the mind the eye of the soul. But one who knows divine wisdom yet yields to evil, speaking harmful words instead of good, unwilling to return and be saved—will not see wickedness leave his bodily house; instead, evil and depravity stay fixed in him, awaiting final evil on the day of God’s anger. Earth-formed body by Lord = our house here. Immovable house = anger/tribulation not leaving home, sent by Lord via humans/demons against those who repay good with evil, to the good person.

If evil-for-evil payer is lawless, how much more evil-for-good payer? Such was Israel in wilderness; Moses in Deut: “Crooked, perverse generation, repay Lord thus?” Beginning = knowledge; righteousness follows knowledge (from knowledge righteousness born); deficiency = ignorance; strife/battle = all wickedness; precedes ignorance = wickedness.

Why accuse poor again? Leading us from idleness; so authority not from hand-laying; thus to walk boldly, be just; strife/battle precede deficiency = lack of virtue in wrongdoers.

Like one calling bitter sweet, sweet bitter; light darkness, darkness light. Here riches = wisdom/knowledge; but to fool, what has wisdom/knowledge learning come? As vine can’t grow in thorns, so in folly wisdom can’t bear fruit; riches = foolish person’s, things concerning each particular matter.
pass_b_english:
It will be, according to the analogy of the feeding, that to each of the brethren is given spiritual knowledge; and so Paul, on the one hand, gave milk to drink to those in Corinth, on the other hand, nourished those in Ephesus with more solid food, speaking concerning height and length and width and depth; and by means of these distinctions he indicates the division of the rational nature, which division encompasses the discourses concerning God's judgment and providence, which discourses are very deeply rooted and lead away from the human condition. Furnaces are the trials; for by means of the trials God elects the warm and the sluggish hearts of the elect. The heretic obeys the tongue of the doctrines of the godless; but those of the Church do not even pay attention. By means of obeying, the voluntary is shown, as if erring into God's wise governance. –This one obeys the tongues of the lawless, he who receives unjust calculations from them and hastens to act according to them; concerning these the righteous is said not to pay attention, to see both the visible and the invisible, that is, not to nourish oneself further within. The faithful, he says, will see the words of this world, which they have figuratively presented as nourishment to the mind; but the unbeliever will not even know the word of any chance thing, on account of the uncleanness of his own soul; for that the wealth of the soul is the knowledge of God, Paul teaches, saying: You have been enriched in everything, in all knowledge and in all wisdom; but if anyone wishes to show that this conception is not this one of mine,

Let those who possess wealth speak of where they acquired their riches—the ones who wandered about in sheepskins and goatskins, destitute, afflicted, and tormented; how, too, can the unbeliever not possess even a single obol, while many unbelievers, cloaked in great wealth, I mean kings and rulers of this world, abound in riches? Faithful lips declare the virtuous thoughts; but to the foolish, evil thoughts will be acceptable. For what partnership has righteousness with injustice? Unless, perhaps, one who has repented seeks discernment and faith. Through righteousness, we conceal iniquity; through self-control, we conceal intemperance; and again, through love, we conceal hatred; and through freedom from love of money, we conceal greed—yes, the greed quantified as 17.200. We also conceal arrogance through humility, and ferocity through meekness, as we seek spiritual friendship, which signifies holy knowledge; and according to Paul, certain ones among the saints are called fellow citizens, and natives of the heavenly Jerusalem, having been built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets. He says here that the body is the house of the soul; and again, the soul is the house of the mind; and the same mind is called the eye of the soul. But the one who has learned divine knowledge and wisdom, yet has surrendered himself to wickedness, and instead of good words brings forth evil ones, and is unwilling to turn back and be saved—such a person will not see wickedness and depravity depart from the house of his body; rather, they remain firmly entrenched within him, so that complete evil may come upon him, abiding immovable within him on the day of the Lord’s wrath.

The body formed from the earth by the Lord for us, he says, is a house here; and the one that will not be moved, that is, will not depart from its own house, is anger and tribulation, sent forth by men and demons by the Lord, against those who repay good with evil, to the good-doer himself, a human being.

If one who repays evil for evil is lawless, how much more so is one who repays evil for good? Such a one became Israel in the wilderness; to whom Moses says in Deuteronomy: “A crooked and perverse generation, do you repay the Lord thus?” Here he says the beginning is knowledge; and righteousness follows knowledge, for righteousness is begotten from knowledge; but deficiency is ignorance; and strife and battle, every wickedness, precedes ignorance, the wickedness.

Why then do you again accuse the poor? By leading us away from idleness; therefore authority does not come from the laying on of hands; hence, if you wish to walk with boldness, you must be just; and strife and battle precede deficiency, that is, the lack of virtue in those who do wrong.

Such is the one who says the bitter is sweet and the sweet is bitter; and who calls light darkness, and darkness light. Here riches are said to be wisdom and knowledge; but to the foolish, what has the learning of wisdom and knowledge come to? For as a vine cannot grow in thorns, so in folly wisdom cannot bear fruit; for riches are the foolish person’s, the things concerning each particular matter of his.
